analysis.title: GS Kamshad - GS TMT TODAY 10.26.26
key_insights: Futures are about flat (NDX and S&P each +10bps) with crude -2%, ahead of a busy week. Central bank decisions include the FOMC, BOC, ECB and BOJ, and 44% of SPX market cap reports, led by MSFT, GOOG, AMZN and INTC.
Brazil's President Lula came from behind to win the presidential runoff with ~51.8% of the vote. EWZ is down 25% in the pre-market.

Middle East de-escalation: Iran will reportedly host top officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey for regional security talks. France avoided a downgrade at Moody's, which produced a relief rally.

AI capital raising is a growing talking point given the industry's capital needs and stress in the bond and convert markets. Musk said SpaceX closed $40bn of debt for GPUs and that debt markets have almost entirely shut off access for companies without substantial revenue independent of AI data centers. He expects the 200+ neoclouds to face heavy death and consolidation. CRWV is -5%.

SK Hynix reportedly plans a special dividend of about 16 trillion won ($12bn) from the 20 trillion won gain on its Kioxia stake booked in 1H. It is also weighing a 50-60 trillion won package that includes a potential buyback. Details are due with earnings Wednesday. Its shares bucked a broad selloff in AI-related stocks.

Hatzius (GIR): 2026 global growth has been in line with potential GDP. Fiscal easing and the AI boom offset the Iran war and US tariff drag. Risks to growth are tilted to the downside because gasoline, diesel, jet fuel and European/Asian natural gas prices are near or above their March/April highs.

Prime Services: S&P 500 fell -0.5% on the week. US equities were net sold for a 3rd straight week (4 of the last 5), with the largest single-stock de-grossing since late July. HFs sold Industrials at the fastest pace in 6+ months, while Staples and Real Estate were the most net bought sectors, a defensive posture.

The GS floor saw ~$20bn of net TMT selling over 2 weeks, approaching the -$23bn over 2 weeks in the July AI selling episode. Little rotation into defensive pockets was seen this week, unlike the prior week.

Managed Money added Brent call positions: 32% of the $2.3bn new gross longs from Oct 6-13 were calls, and a further ~$1bn was bought through Oct 20. Brent put-call skew cheapened, and dealers appear incrementally shorter gamma to the upside.

Thursday saw capitulation and de-grossing on AI financing worries and geopolitical escalation. The GS Risk Appetite Indicator had one of its largest drops on record and is at its lowest since April of last year. Vol of vol is at the 83rd percentile (3-year lookback), and the NDX-SPX implied vol spread is near 5-year highs (98th percentile).

GS Baskets view: the market is in an HF deleveraging episode where short-term stops matter more than medium-term value. GS recommends buying the dip and repositioning selectively into AI, starting with Power, Hyperscalers, Inference and Cyber. The AI vs AI-At-Risk pair (GSPUARTI) is down 13% YTD and SPXXAI has overtaken the S&P 500 YTD.

Sector specialists: NDX finished the week -80bps, the GS TMT Broad AI Basket was -4.1% and the TMT Mo' Basket -7.8%. Earnings have not stabilized sentiment (META, LRCX, TTMI, WDC sold off on results). Investors are looking for catalysts (the election, easing macro headwinds, AI datapoints), and appetite for non-AI idiosyncratic TMT ideas is rising.

DUOL Q3'26 preview: the debate is shifting from user growth reacceleration to whether engagement converts to bookings growth and monetization. Q2 DAU growth accelerated to +23% YoY with record retention.

650 Group (Weckel) forecasts the DC networking market to grow at a 29% 5-yr CAGR from 2030-35. It expects x86 server unit growth driven by AI agents and strong ASPs from higher memory costs. It is more cautious on enterprise/campus networking beyond 2027 (demographics, Huawei in EMEA, Ubiquiti up market).

Street actions: TSLA upgraded to Overweight (Barclays). EFX downgraded to Sector Perform (RBC), SPOT to Accumulate (Phillip Secs), XYZ to Equal-Weight (Morgan Stanley). NTNX initiated at Buy and NTAP at Neutral (Guggenheim).

Event calendar: FOMC Wed 10/28 (WIRP 11% chance of hike), Thu 10/29 core PCE (consensus +30bps m/m), GDP, ECB and BOJ decisions. Hyperscaler earnings (MSFT, GOOGL on Wed; AMZN on Thu) plus INTC, SNDK, STX and SK Hynix are the key semis and AI reads.
